scope.summary:
Rebuild, as native Rust Handshake tools hosted in the WP-KERNEL-011 shell, the two editor surfaces that currently exist as React (KERNEL-009 'Notes'): (1) the VS-Code-class CODE editor and (2) the Obsidian/Notion-class RICH-TEXT + knowledge editor. Achieve FULL feature parity with what KERNEL-009 already delivered in React, then make them deeply interconnect with each other and with CKC (Pillar 18/19 + KERNEL-005) and Loom (Pillar 7). REUSE the existing Rust backend (handshake_core: knowledge documents, loom, code-nav, CRDT, search) - do NOT rebuild backend storage/APIs. The legacy React editors (app/src) stay as the parity reference until native parity is proven, then are retired. No new future surfaces (Photoshop/Affinity/spreadsheet/engines) are built here; the editors must expose clean extension seams so those plug in later. EXPANSION 2026-06-21: the editors are the Notes pillar (native, not stitched-on apps) and MUST melt together with FEMS (Pillar 12 typed memory), Stage (Pillar 17), Calendar (Pillar 2), and Locus (Pillar 6) in addition to CKC + Loom (E9/E10); continue the WP-KERNEL-011 GUI by wiring the disabled editor-orbit shell placeholders to the real editors (E11); and complete a structured Settings menu + built-in manual for the editors (E12). All pillar-interop is backend-reuse-only (typed blockers for gaps).

[SCOPE ADJUSTMENT 2026-06-27] This WP is ALSO expanded to build Handshake+'+s three-tier diagnostic substrate decoupled from the Flight Recorder (v02.196 §5.8 internal_diagnostics + §6.13 Palmistry), as MT-081..MT-096 on the same ultracode pipeline. internal_diagnostics = in-app self-diagnostics; Palmistry = external out-of-process watcher that survives freezes/crashes; FR kept as-is (no schema re-open). Records NO project/sensitive data (typed allowlist).

[SCOPE EXPANSION #2 2026-06-27] This WP is FURTHER expanded (MT-097..MT-104) to make Handshake usable as the product: a notes work-surface with a chatbox beside it (Obsidian + VS Code/Cursor/Antigravity model), with the non-notes feature windows stripped from the default layout for now (rewired per-feature later); plus terminal + local/cloud model launch inside a repo folder with the correct wrapper; plus a working visual debugger + FOREGROUND-SAFE front-end navigation (no operator mouse/keyboard steal) so models can test in-app; plus the internal manual. Built AFTER the diagnostic MTs 081-096.

src/backend/** (reuse via existing API/IPC only; backend changes are out of scope and must be raised as a typed blocker)

acceptance_criteria: CODE editor reaches parity with the existing React Monaco surface: syntax highlighting (tree-sitter), large-file performance, multi-cursor/column-select, find/replace, code folding, minimap/outline, go-to-line, and LSP (completion/hover/go-to-def/references/diagnostics). Proven against the same scenarios the React version passed.

RICH-TEXT editor reaches parity with the existing React Tiptap surface: block document model, headings/lists/tables/quotes/code-blocks, embeds (image/slideshow/album/video), wikilinks + transclusion, slash commands, properties panel, find/replace, daily notes, and save-to-format (HTML/md/txt/JSON).

Obsidian-class knowledge surface parity: local + global graph, folder tree + color labels, tags + tag hubs, pins/favorites/backlinks/unlinked, breadcrumbs, wiki-page projection, canvas board placing real Loom blocks, and block-collection views (table/Kanban/calendar).
Search parity: Loom Search v2 surface (full-text + fuzzy + semantic, graph-blended, results-as-saved-view), find-in-files, and quick-switcher integration - all bound to the existing backend.

INTERCONNECTION (the core deliverable): the two editors and CKC and Loom melt together - shared selection/clipboard/command bus across surfaces; everything is addressable as a Loom block with live backlinks; CKC media/characters/moodboards can be embedded/dragged into notes and canvas and routed to Stage; code and notes can cross-reference; one unified undo + one event-ledger across surfaces. Proven by interconnection scenario tests.

Backend reuse proven: editors read/write through the EXISTING handshake_core APIs (knowledge documents, loom, code-nav, CRDT) with no backend rewrite; any backend gap is a typed blocker, not an in-WP backend change.
Model-vision parity: every editor + knowledge action is exposed via the WP-011 AccessKit surface so a swarm agent can author/edit code and notes and drive the graph/canvas by stable id; proven.

Full-parity proof suite: a runtime suite maps each KERNEL-009-delivered feature to a passing native proof (the parity gate); performance proven on large docs; interconnection proven; zero placeholders/mocks for spec-required runtime behavior.

interconnection_contract.principle: CX-003-VIS / CX-004-VIS: everything melts together, everything accesses everything; handmade primitives share one selection, undo, event ledger, and model-accessibility model.
edges: RichText <-> Code: open a code block/file from a note in the code editor; reference code symbols from notes; shared find/replace and command bus.
Editors <-> Loom: every document/block/canvas node is a Loom block with content hash + backlinks; Loom Search v2 indexes all of it; AI Loom jobs propose tags/links across surfaces.

Editors <-> CKC (Studio/Atelier/KERNEL-005): drag CKC media/characters/worldbuilding/moodboards into a note or canvas as embeds; route a note/selection to a Stage pane; CKC artifacts appear in the same library and search.

Shared substrate: one selection model, one clipboard, one command palette/registry, one undo stack scope policy, one event ledger (Flight Recorder), one AccessKit model-surface across all editor panes.

Editors <-> FEMS (Pillar 12): consume the retrieval capsule / MemoryPack inline (provenance-first, <=500 tokens, <=24 items); emit review-gated memory-write proposals with document_id + selection-range + content-hash provenance (FR-EVT-MEM-001). Commit stays review-gated, never editor-direct.
Editors <-> Stage (Pillar 17): route a note/selection/canvas-node to a Stage pane; embed Stage capture artifacts back into notes/canvas as MT-014 embeds with SHA-256 manifest provenance.
Editors <-> Calendar (Pillar 2): daily notes bind to CalendarEvents by date; read-only ActivitySpan correlation surfaces which documents were edited during a calendar block.
Editors <-> Locus (Pillar 6): notes and code cross-reference WP/MT records via locus:// addressing reusing the everything-is-a-block scheme, with reverse lookup of referencing documents.
Editors <-> WP-011 shell: all editor actions route through the existing menu / command bus / unified undo / context-menu / status-bar / settings / manual substrate (extension, not fork).
Future extension seams (designed, NOT built): image/photo editor (Photoshop/Affinity), spreadsheet, mechanical engines - all attach to the same block/selection/event/accessibility substrate.

mt_plan.stall_detection_expansion_note: WP SCOPE EXPANSION #3 (operator 2026-06-28): MT-105/106 = make the hours-long SILENT HANG that just wasted operator time IMPOSSIBLE inside Handshake. Generalize freeze detection from Handshake+'+s own UI thread to ANY operation + spawned subprocess, caught by BOTH internal_diagnostics and Palmistry. MT-105 internal_diagnostics OPERATION/SUBPROCESS STALL WATCHDOG: any in-app operation (backend call, spawned terminal/model session MT-100/101, tool run, workflow step) registers a deadline + periodic progress heartbeat; a stall past the deadline WITHOUT progress emits a typed StalledOperation diagnostic + surfaces it (Settings->Diagnostics + status) within a BOUNDED time - never silent. MT-106 Palmistry CHILD-PROCESS STALL WATCH + end-to-end NO-SILENT-HANG proof: Palmistry watches the child processes Handshake SPAWNS (sessions/tools/terminals/models), detecting a hung child (alive but no progress) the same way it detects Handshake+'+s freeze + surfacing it; the capstone proof spawns a DELIBERATELY-hung operation AND a deliberately-hung child and asserts internal_diagnostics emits StalledOperation AND Palmistry surfaces the hung child, BOTH within a bounded time (seconds, not hours). ORDER: implemented AFTER the current diagnostic (081-096) + usability (097-104) MTs; created now so state is not lost. depends_on: 105 -> internal_diagnostics tier (082-088); 106 -> Palmistry (089-094) + 105.

open_items.finding: Running three sub-agents concurrently inside ONE product worktree materially degrades source-provenance-bound proofs. Several MTs (notably MT-027, MT-066, MT-068) bind their official proof to an exact committed HEAD, but while other agents hold uncommitted edits no agent can bind a clean tree. Observed concretely: the MT-029 run5 compiled input is NOT byte-identical to HEAD b0d84cfc because the tree simultaneously held MT-079 uncommitted app.rs edits and MT-111 uncommitted event_emitter.rs edits. The MT-029 agent handled this correctly and honestly - it recorded the exact dirty set to mt029_run5_source_state.txt and will report the matrix as bound to HEAD PLUS a named delta rather than falsely claiming a clean-HEAD binding.
secondary_symptoms: Agents repeatedly block on the SHARED ~/.cargo package-cache lock, which scoped CARGO_TARGET_DIR does not isolate; observed blocking three cargo invocations at once.

Agents have had to commit each other in-flight work (5968bb36, 110389fd, fcf49702) purely so a source-bound gate could bind a clean HEAD - work is preserved, but authorship attribution in the history becomes muddled.
One agent mid-edit file broke another agent build for roughly 15 minutes.
open_items.mitigations_applied_so_far: Every brief now instructs agents to wait and retry on lock contention rather than conclude a product defect, to never kill a process they did not start, and to keep shared-file edits additive and disclosed. KERNEL_BUILDER committed the tree once (5dc08b0f) to give the gated MTs a clean HEAD.
open_items.recommended_fix: For the REMAINING source-provenance-bound MTs, SERIALIZE: run at most one agent whose proof binds an exact committed HEAD, and let concurrent agents work only on MTs whose proofs are not source-bound. The alternative - one worktree per concurrent MT - is forbidden here because KERNEL_BUILDER_PROTOCOL restricts worktree creation to the WP activation phase and the WP worktree budget is 1 per WP.

open_items.finding: Concurrent cargo/rustc compilation starves PostgreSQL disk I/O badly enough to make live proofs fail with what LOOKS like a product defect. Root-caused by the MT-029 agent from retained artifacts rather than guessed.
evidence: reqwest reported is_timeout=true, is_connect=false, is_status=false - the connection was accepted and the response never came, so the backend was reachable.
The retained failure-diagnostics.json recorded immediate_health = {http_status:200, status:ok, db_status:ok} AT THE MOMENT OF FAILURE.

The backend own stdout log shows single-row statements taking seconds on the seeding path: INSERT INTO loom_block_search_index elapsed=8.7647135s; INSERT INTO knowledge_rich_document_versions elapsed=1.2497329s; SELECT FROM knowledge_document_backlinks elapsed=1.6248237s; SELECT FROM loom_edges elapsed=1.5319158s. NOT database bloat: the WP-scoped DB is 37 MB with 1 rich document and 4 workspaces, so cleanup is working.

open_items.finding: The bounds carried by nodes in the argus.inspect() tree do NOT describe the mounted frame. inspect() -> capture_mcp_snapshot_for_navigation (app.rs:12159) -> refresh_mcp_snapshot(), which renders on a FRESH egui::Context, so the geometry belongs to a synthetic re-render.
open_items.hard_evidence: A containment assertion written during MT-119 read the Restore control right edge as 2605.875px inside a 2560px-wide harness - beyond the entire window - while the GPU frame captured by the SAME run shows both controls comfortably inside the Find-in-Files pane.
open_items.impact: Any geometry, containment, clipping or overlap assertion sourced from the inspect tree is unsound and will produce false positives or false negatives. This is a live risk for HBR-VIS acceptance and for the MT-108 pixel-row gates, which reason about what is materially visible.
open_items.known_sibling_hazard: The same fresh-context render is already known to make egui::Memory-backed state (popup and context menus) read back EMPTY. The bounds consequence is newly recorded here.
open_items.recommended_fix: Either expose the mounted rects through a dedicated product seam, or restrict visual acceptance to the captured frame itself. Additionally, document in the internal manual that inspect-tree bounds are NOT operator-visible geometry, so no future MT builds a proof on them.

kernel_builder_root_cause.mechanism: The test stands up its OWN deterministic 404 server on an EPHEMERAL port (it reads listener.local_addr(), so a fixed-port collision is ruled out - that was the obvious hypothesis and it is wrong). The server thread runs a hard 10-SECOND deadline and panics with "memory-pack 404 was not requested" if the shell has not issued the memory-pack read by then. That is the unnamed-thread panic seen at test_app_host_mount_secondary.rs:3540 in the full-binary run.
kernel_builder_root_cause.why_it_fails_only_in_the_full_binary: cargo runs the binary 51 tests in PARALLEL by default. Under that load the shell does not reach its FEMS refresh-for-context within the fixed 10s window, the server thread dies on its deadline, and the downstream assertion ever_in_flight (AC-080-5) then fails. Run alone, the read fires immediately - observed printing "relevant_memory: ever_requested=true got_blocker=true" and passing 1/0.
kernel_builder_root_cause.classification: TEST ROBUSTNESS under parallelism, NOT a product defect and NOT MT-113 fallout. The product behaviour it asserts (the shell drives the FEMS read, and a 404 surfaces as a typed blocker) is demonstrably correct when given time.
kernel_builder_root_cause.how_to_fix_without_weakening_anything: Do NOT relax the ASSERTIONS - ever_in_flight and the typed blocker are the real contract and must stay. The 10s wall-clock deadline is the fragile part. Prefer making the wait condition-based with a generous bound, or serialising this test, over simply enlarging the constant. Note MT-113 hit a sibling of this class and solved it properly with an explicit quiescence gate rather than a longer sleep - the same instinct applies here.
kernel_builder_root_cause.impact_on_the_capstone: MT-108 item 11 requires the full suite to pass. A test that is green alone and red in its own binary makes that sweep NON-DETERMINISTIC, so this must be fixed before the capstone rather than discovered inside it. Recording it now is the difference between a known 10-minute fix and an unexplained capstone failure.

RESOLVED.fix: Widened the server ANTI-HANG GUARD from 10s to 120s in tests/test_app_host_mount_secondary.rs, with the reasoning documented at the site.
RESOLVED.precise_root_cause: The two bounds were mismatched in KIND: the client loop is ITERATION-bounded (80 x run_steps(2) plus a 25ms sleep) while the server guard was TIME-bounded at 10s. Under cargo default 51-way parallelism the client fixed iterations outlast a 10s clock, the server thread panics, and server.join() converts that into a failure of an otherwise-correct test.
RESOLVED.hypothesis_checked_and_rejected: A fixed-port collision between parallel tests was the obvious explanation and is WRONG - the server binds an EPHEMERAL port via listener.local_addr(). Verified in source before changing anything.
RESOLVED.nothing_weakened: No assertion was relaxed. ever_in_flight (AC-080-5) and the typed blocker remain exactly as written, and the widened guard CANNOT mask a defect: if the shell never issues the read, the client loop still completes and ever_in_flight still fails.
RESOLVED.verified: cargo test --test test_app_host_mount_secondary => EXIT 0, 51 passed / 0 failed (was 50 passed / 1 failed).
RESOLVED.capstone_impact: One source of MT-108 full-suite non-determinism is removed.

ledger_evidence_2_of_3.method: Queried the ledger DIRECTLY rather than inferring from the test: SELECT event_type, actor_id, count(*) FROM kernel_event_ledger WHERE actor_id LIKE 'handshake-native:%' GROUP BY 1,2. This reads what the product actually wrote, independent of the test filter.
ledger_evidence_2_of_3.result: EVERY run produces exactly 2 FLIGHT_RECORDER_MIRROR_PENDING and 2 FLIGHT_RECORDER_MIRROR_RECORDED rows - never 3. Confirmed across FOUR DISTINCT process identities: pid 33100 (the run observed failing), 103896, 106768 and 84720.
ledger_evidence_2_of_3.conclusion: The shortfall is REPRODUCIBLE AND HISTORICAL, not a flake and not caused by anything landed tonight. Two of the three expected emissions reach the EventLedger mirror; the third never does. Each mirrored event yields one PENDING plus one RECORDED row, so 2+2 means exactly two events, matching the test seeing fewer than three.
ledger_evidence_2_of_3.what_this_rules_out: Not contention (idle machine, deterministic). Not authorization (MT-109 gating is satisfied - the rows carry server-derived handshake-native:{pid}:{birth} actors). Not workspace scoping (wsids is populated). Not MT-113 fallout (the shortfall predates tonight, visible in older process identities). The defect is that a third emission never lands.
ledger_evidence_2_of_3.most_likely_owner: MT-111 rewired this emitter. The test comment at test_event_emitter.rs:2271 records that MT-111 removed actor_id as client authority and the test was rewritten to scope by workspace. A plausible reading is that MT-111 left the test expecting three emissions where the rewired emitter now produces two - which would make the TEST stale rather than the product broken, exactly like MT-114. That is a HYPOTHESIS and must be proven either way.
ledger_evidence_2_of_3.instruction_for_the_agent: Determine WHICH of the three emissions is absent and whether the product or the expectation is wrong. If the product is correct and the test is stale, correct the test with a comment citing the evidence, as MT-114 did. If an emission is genuinely lost, that is an MT-111 regression and needs a product fix. finding_2026_09_04_surql_line_endings.owner: UNASSIGNED - needs its own microtask, deliberately not folded into MT-145 or MT-146
finding_2026_09_04_surql_line_endings.finding: `.gitattributes` declares `text eol=lf` for .md, .mjs, .json and a long list of governance paths, but never for `*.surql`. `git check-attr text eol` on src/backend/handshake_core/src/storage/surreal/schema.surql returns `unspecified`, so a fresh checkout on Windows materialises those files with CRLF.
finding_2026_09_04_surql_line_endings.why_it_matters: The product `include_str!`s the .surql files in four places and hashes their bytes for a compiled-manifest check. A CRLF copy therefore fails `verify_compiled_manifest`, and the embedded SurrealDB store never bootstraps. Every embedded test in that worktree fails at the schema gate before any assertion runs, which masks whatever the tests were actually written to prove.
finding_2026_09_04_surql_line_endings.how_it_surfaced: Creating the wtc-k12-mt145 worktree for the MT-145 lane on 2026-09-04. The long-lived wtc-native-editors-v1 worktree is unaffected because it was checked out when the files were already LF on disk, so this defect is invisible until someone makes a new worktree.
finding_2026_09_04_surql_line_endings.evidence: git check-attr text eol -- src/backend/handshake_core/src/storage/surreal/schema.surql => text: unspecified, eol: unspecified. Both .surql files show zero changed lines under `git diff` after normalisation, semantic and raw, with only the 'LF will be replaced by CRLF' advisory, confirming the difference is byte-level line endings and not content.
finding_2026_09_04_surql_line_endings.interim_mitigation: The MT-145 lane normalised the two affected files to LF in its own worktree only. That change is deliberately NEVER staged or committed: it lies outside MT-145's allowed paths, schema.surql belongs to MT-146, and committing a line-ending flip would renormalise the files on the branch and could break the other lane. It is disclosed in MT-145's implementation result as an environmental repair.
finding_2026_09_04_surql_line_endings.durable_fix_not_yet_applied: Adding `*.surql text eol=lf` to .gitattributes is a one-line change, but it renormalises files repo-wide and would touch every .surql in the tree. That deserves its own microtask with a deliberate renormalisation step and a verification that the compiled-manifest hashes still match, rather than being smuggled into a test-harness lane.
finding_2026_09_04_surql_line_endings.do_not_lose: Anyone creating a new product worktree on Windows will hit this and will most likely misdiagnose it as a schema or migration defect, because the symptom is a schema-drift assertion rather than anything mentioning line endings.

finding_2026_09_05_shared_cargo_target.owner: UNASSIGNED - repo tooling, outside every current microtask scope
finding_2026_09_05_shared_cargo_target.finding: Two places default cargo builds into ONE shared, unscoped target directory, so any two lanes running at once contend on a single cargo file lock. (1) .cargo/config.toml at the repo root sets target-dir = "../Handshake_Artifacts/handshake-cargo-target", which every build inherits unless it explicitly overrides CARGO_TARGET_DIR. (2) The governed MT auto-relay hook, .GOV/roles_shared/scripts/hooks/post-commit-mt-review-request.mjs, hardcodes the same path at line 128 and runs cargo check inline at line 121 on any commit with a feat: MT-NNN subject.
finding_2026_09_05_shared_cargo_target.precision_correction: The implementing agent reported this as landing in "the directory CX-984-002 forbids". That overstates it and a validator would chase the wrong thing. Verified: the path resolves to Handshake Worktrees/Handshake_Artifacts/handshake-cargo-target, which IS the permitted artifacts root. The defect is that it is SHARED and unscoped, not that it is forbidden. The genuinely forbidden siblings are Handshake/Handshake_Artifacts and Handshake Worktrees/handshake-cargo-target, and neither is in play here.
finding_2026_09_05_shared_cargo_target.why_it_matters: The hook is the sharper half. It runs a compile gate inline on the shared target dir, so a concurrent lane holding that lock can starve it into the TIMEOUT_INCONCLUSIVE branch at line 150 - which tells the validator to treat compile evidence as inconclusive. The governed auto-relay can therefore be made to emit a degraded verdict by unrelated work simply running at the same time. That is a governance-tooling defect, not a product one.
finding_2026_09_05_shared_cargo_target.observed_this_session: Three lanes ran concurrently. Every one had to be given an owner-scoped CARGO_TARGET_DIR by hand to avoid contending, and the operator had to be told explicitly why. The MT-146 lane also deliberately sequenced its product build after its suite for exactly this reason, and one false negative was already attributed to this class of starvation.
finding_2026_09_05_shared_cargo_target.suggested_scope: Decide whether the default should be owner-scoped (per worktree or per lane) rather than shared, and make the hook use a scoped dir or skip its inline compile gate when the lock is held rather than timing out into an inconclusive verdict.
finding_2026_09_05_shared_cargo_target.evidence: Verified by the orchestrator: cat .cargo/config.toml resolving to Handshake Worktrees/Handshake_Artifacts/handshake-cargo-target; and grep of post-commit-mt-review-request.mjs showing the cargo check at line 121, the hardcoded CARGO_TARGET_DIR at line 128, and the TIMEOUT_INCONCLUSIVE branch at line 150.

cargo_target_dir_convention_2026_09_05.instruction_source: Operator, 2026-09-05: create a subfolder per work packet and per microtask for cargo checks.
cargo_target_dir_convention_2026_09_05.convention: Handshake Worktrees/Handshake_Artifacts/handshake-cargo-target/<wp-slug>/<mt-slug>/ — for this packet, k12/m145, k12/m146, k12/m147, k12/m148, plus k12/shared for work not bound to one microtask. Every lane sets CARGO_TARGET_DIR to its own leaf and never to a parent.
cargo_target_dir_convention_2026_09_05.why_the_slugs_are_short_and_not_the_full: The literal form, WP-KERNEL-012/MT-146, would break the build. Measured on this host: the deepest existing artifact path under a 10-character slug is 252 characters against the MSVC 260 limit, leaving 8 characters of headroom. The full identifiers cost 20 characters against the current 10, which lands at or past 260 and reproduces the C1083 failure in the bundled DuckDB C++ headers. Enabling long paths in the registry does not help cl.exe. The short form k12/m146 is 8 characters, so it is two characters SHORTER than the flat slug it replaces and gains headroom while adding the structure the Operator asked for.
cargo_target_dir_convention_2026_09_05.what_it_fixes: The shared-target-dir contention recorded in finding_2026_09_05_shared_cargo_target. Concurrent lanes stop serialising on one cargo file lock, which is what forced three lanes this session to be assigned scoped directories by hand and what starved at least one build into a false negative.
cargo_target_dir_convention_2026_09_05.what_it_does_not_fix: The two defaults themselves. .cargo/config.toml still points every unscoped build at the shared root, and the MT auto-relay post-commit hook still hardcodes it and runs cargo check inline, where a concurrent lock holder can starve it into TIMEOUT_INCONCLUSIVE. This convention governs lanes that set CARGO_TARGET_DIR deliberately; it does not change what happens when nobody sets it. That remains open and unassigned.
cargo_target_dir_convention_2026_09_05.migration_rule: Do not move a lane that is mid-build. A running cargo invocation holds its target dir; repointing it discards the work and can corrupt the cache. Adopt the new leaf at the next cold start, or immediately for any lane not currently building. Warm directories may be seeded by copying an existing warm one - proven this session, cargo accepts a relocated target dir.

finding_2026_09_05_suite_livelock.owner: UNASSIGNED - test harness; related to but distinct from the MT-123 teardown defect
finding_2026_09_05_suite_livelock.finding: The in-crate api::memory:: suite livelocks at DEFAULT libtest parallelism when the host is carrying other cargo work. Measured: 29 tests launched simultaneously at 23:45:39, each opening its own embedded RocksDB store, 26 store directories created in one burst and none afterwards. After 3.8 hours only 4 of 29 tests had completed and 25 were sitting in the has-been-running-for-over-60-seconds state.
finding_2026_09_05_suite_livelock.why_it_is_not_simply_the_teardown_drain: An earlier run of this same suite completed in 2255 seconds at the same parallelism with the same 30-second teardown drain per store. The drain alone therefore does not explain it. The variable is host contention: with nine cargo and rustc processes resident from other lanes, 26-way concurrent store access turns ordinary contention into a livelock rather than a slowdown.
finding_2026_09_05_suite_livelock.how_it_disguises_itself: Every outward signal says healthy. The process is alive, CPU is non-zero and advancing, and no error is emitted. Two things give it away, and neither is visible without deliberately looking: no new store directory is created after the initial burst, and the working set collapses (2.6 GB down to 0.3 GB) as the tests stop doing work. Log output is also block-buffered when redirected, so the log itself looks frozen and gives no help either way.
finding_2026_09_05_suite_livelock.orchestrator_error_worth_recording: I initially accepted a non-zero CPU delta as proof the run was progressing, and agreed to let it continue on that basis. Advancing and making progress through the suite are different claims and I let the first stand in for the second, which cost additional waiting. The store-directory count is the signal that actually distinguishes them.
finding_2026_09_05_suite_livelock.mitigation_that_works: Cap libtest concurrency. The MT-145 lane ran both its suites at --test-threads=4 under the same host load and completed. The MT-146 lane relaunched at 4 after the stall. Serial (--test-threads=1) is not the answer either: the fixed teardown cost alone would put this suite near two hours.
finding_2026_09_05_suite_livelock.suggested_scope: Decide whether these suites should carry a default thread cap in configuration rather than relying on every operator to pass it, and whether the embedded store harness should bound concurrent stores directly. Pairs naturally with the MT-123 teardown work and with the shared cargo target dir finding, since all three are about concurrent lanes interfering.
finding_2026_09_05_suite_livelock.evidence: Log section with 4 ok lines and 25 over-60-seconds lines; store-directory creation timestamps under Handshake_Artifacts/handshake-test/storage-conformance showing 26 at 23:45:39 and none after; CPU sampling of the test binary at 17 percent of one core with working set collapsed to 0.3 GB at 3.82 hours elapsed.

finding_2026_09_05_concurrent_commit_fla.the_mechanism_that_is_still_open: The implementer identified a credible way its change could widen the window without being the cause. commit_memory_proposal calls reconcile_workspace_memory_commit_events, which is workspace-scoped, so two concurrent commits reconcile the same rows. The listing-gate removal means each pass now returns FR-EVT-MEM-004 alongside its FR-EVT-MEM-003 rather than deferring it, so both loops contend over more rows per pass. A project_commit_event failure propagates through reconcile(...)? and surfaces as exactly this 500. Not deterministic and not mine are different claims; only the first is established.
finding_2026_09_05_concurrent_commit_fla.why_it_matters_beyond_the_flake: A 500 internal_error is the outer wrapper. Whatever it wrapped is a real failure mode in the concurrent commit path that only appears under contention, and nobody has yet read what it was. The flake is the symptom worth chasing, not the thing to suppress.
finding_2026_09_05_concurrent_commit_fla.what_not_to_do: Do not close this by re-running until a green suite appears and quoting that. AC-146-5 wants 29 of 29, and a 29/0 obtained by retry, reported without the flake, would be worse than an honest 28/1.

finding_2026_09_05_backup_push_repoints_.finding: node .GOV/roles_shared/scripts/topology/backup-push.mjs <local> <backup> repoints the LOCAL branch upstream at the backup branch. Observed verbatim: "branch feat/WP-KERNEL-012 set up to track origin/backup/WP-KERNEL-012-wtc-dirt-20260905". The backup itself worked correctly.
finding_2026_09_05_backup_push_repoints_.why_it_is_a_trap: After a backup push, a bare git push from the working branch targets the BACKUP branch rather than the feature branch. Any lane that pushes without an explicit refspec would silently land its work on a backup ref, where nothing downstream reads it, and the push would report success. This packet only escaped it because every agent was instructed to push with an explicit refspec.
finding_2026_09_05_backup_push_repoints_.compounding_factor: remote.origin.fetch in the product worktree is narrowed to +refs/heads/gov_kernel:refs/remotes/origin/gov_kernel, so git will not accept origin/feat/WP-KERNEL-012 as a tracking branch even when that ref exists locally. Repairing the upstream after a backup push therefore fails through the normal --set-upstream-to path and needs the branch.<name>.remote and branch.<name>.merge config written directly.
finding_2026_09_05_backup_push_repoints_.what_i_did: Restored branch.feat/WP-KERNEL-012.remote=origin and branch.feat/WP-KERNEL-012.merge=refs/heads/feat/WP-KERNEL-012 by direct config write, then confirmed an explicit push dry-run reports Everything up-to-date against the feature branch. The backup branch remains on the remote at 6d5d705f as intended.
finding_2026_09_05_backup_push_repoints_.suggested_scope: backup-push should either restore the original upstream after pushing, or use a push refspec that does not set tracking at all. Neither the backup nor the working branch needs the upstream changed for the backup to be created.
finding_2026_09_05_backup_push_repoints_.evidence: backup-push.mjs run output on 2026-09-05 creating backup/WP-KERNEL-012-wtc-dirt-20260905; the subsequent git rev-parse --abbrev-ref @{u} failures; git config --get-all remote.origin.fetch showing the single gov_kernel refspec.

approved_texts.VPX-011: - [VPX-011] Stable round source path: each owner builds every round from ONE fixed export directory (`<owner-target-or-artifact-root>/export-current`), never from a per-candidate path such as `export-<sha>`. Cargo hashes path crates outside a manifest's workspace root (sibling `../` path dependencies) by absolute source path and the hash cascades to every dependent crate and test binary, so a new path is a cold rebuild and orphans the old artifacts; this completes [VPX-008]. Refresh the directory in place to the frozen candidate ([CX-VAL-001]) at round start only, with no process using it, under the owner's exclusive ownership ([CX-984-002]): (1) read `export-current.identity` (previous SHA, tree id, file count, manifest sha256); (2) apply `git diff --name-status -z <previous> <candidate>`: delete removed files, extract added and modified files from `git archive <candidate> -- <paths>` with `tar -m` so each changed file carries the current mtime (commit-time mtimes older than the last build make Cargo reuse stale output); never touch unchanged files and never overlay files absent from the candidate; (3) delete the export's own round outputs (`target/nextest`, JUnit) so no stale result survives ([CX-VAL-009]); (4) verify every `git ls-tree -r <candidate>` blob id equals the export file's blob id and no other file exists (excluding the harness `.git` pointer); (5) write `export-current.identity` last (candidate SHA, tree id, file count, manifest sha256). A missing, partial or mismatched identity means full replace of the export directory only (own disposable output, [CX-984-006]) and re-archive. Bind each verdict to the identity record copied into the hashed round log and to `HANDSHAKE_PROOF_SOURCE_SHA`; the path never carries candidate identity, and the `Compiling (...export-<sha>...)` provenance check is replaced by the identity hash. Record per round the compiled-crate and relinked-test-binary counts (HBR-COMPART-002); more than the changed crates and their dependents compiling is a rule defect to report.
approved_texts.KB-CAD-VPX-002: - [KB-CAD-VPX-002] Where a lane builds from an export or second checkout, keep one fixed per-owner source path refreshed in place per [VPX-011]; never create a new source folder per commit.
approved_texts.GLOBAL-VALIDATION-023-025: - [GLOBAL-VALIDATION-023–025] Stable build source location: [023] Build every candidate of a project and owner from one stable source path refreshed in place, never from a new source path per candidate, because build tools that derive artifact identity from the source path treat a new path as a cold build and orphan the old artifacts + [024] When refreshing a warm source tree in place, change only files that differ from the previously built candidate, give every changed file a current modification time, and never restore older commit or archive timestamps over a warm build, so timestamp- or content-based change detection cannot reuse stale output + [025] Bind each result to the exact candidate through an identity record taken at refresh (commit id, tree id, file count, manifest hash); never rely on the source path to carry candidate identity.
